sources: dossier=silent on Adjacent-list completeness policy; doc=run-scope.md:23,42 cite `concept:sub-graph` in Purpose and an invariant, sub-graph.md:15 Adjacent list (graph, delegation, node, node-run, cascade) omits run-scope; corroboration cuts both ways=delegation.md also mentions `concept:run-scope` in its Definition prose ('per concept:run-scope') yet also omits run-scope from its own Adjacent list, suggesting the omission may be a deliberate corpus-wide convention (Adjacent lists direct boundary co-owners, not every concept mentioned in passing) rather than an oversight.
note: The one-directional citation is real, but sub-graph.md explicitly disclaims owning per-invocation run trees (pointing readers to node-run/delegation instead), and delegation.md shows the same passing-mention-without-Adjacent-listing pattern for run-scope — so it is unclear whether this is drift or an intentional 'Adjacent lists boundary neighbors, not every prose-mentioned concept' convention. Question for human: should sub-graph.md (and, for consistency, delegation.md) add concept:run-scope to Adjacent given that sub-graph invocation is what creates a sub-graph RunScope, or is the omission intentional because runtime-execution-context concerns are explicitly routed to node-run/delegation instead?
